title: Dependencies in Multiplex Networks: A Motif Count Approach
summary: Multiplex networks are a powerful framework for representing systems with multiple types of interactions among a common set of entities. Understanding their structure requires statistical tools capturing higher-order cross-layer correlations. We develop a comprehensive framework for estimating and testing dependence in exchangeable multiplex networks through motif counts. We first propose a moment-based estimation methodology that extends the multi-layer stochastic block model network histogram to arbitrary motif counts.
